claims.sentence: Students may qualify for accelerated study under an individual plan based on their program level

For bachelor’s and master’s programs, a student qualifies if they have secondary vocational, higher, or additional education, and/or studied in those programs, and/or have abilities or a development level allowing completion in a shorter time than the standard university term set per federal standards

For the PhD (aspirantura) program, a student qualifies if they have a diploma of completed aspirantura or adjuncture, and/or a candidate of sciences diploma, and/or a doctor of sciences diploma, and/or study in another aspirantura program, and/or have abilities or a development level allowing completion in a shorter time than the standard term set per the educational standard
Increasing the study pace specifically requires a personal application from the student, a decision by the University’s Accreditation Committee, and an order from the University Director
The evidence does not state a specific number of months or years for the reduction
The shortened duration is achieved through defined mechanisms rather than a fixed time reduction

For bachelor’s and master’s programs, the reduction is implemented by crediting results from individual disciplines or modules and/or individual practices completed during secondary vocational, higher, or additional education, and/or by increasing the pace of study

For the PhD program, the reduction is implemented by crediting (via re-examination) fully or partially the results of individual disciplines or modules, and/or individual practices, and/or individual types of scientific research work, and/or by increasing the pace of study
The evidence does not specify how many months or years the degree program will be shortened
The evidence does not define what constitutes "corresponding abilities or development level"
The evidence does not provide the exact procedures, timelines, or forms for the personal application or the Accreditation Committee decision
The evidence does not indicate whether different courses or departments apply different reduction amounts
The evidence does not address what happens if a student’s application is denied
